BMR_BASE_METABOLISM.title: Base Metabolism
BMR_BASE_METABOLISM.body: Your body burns calories just to keep your heart beating and brain running. Never forget to pack for your resting needs!

PANDOLF_WEIGHT_PENALTY.title: The Pandolf Penalty
PANDOLF_WEIGHT_PENALTY.body: The Pandolf Equation shows that carrying a pack increases effort exponentially. A heavy pack can feel twice as heavy on steep terrain!

HYDRATION_BASICS.title: Hydration Fundamentals
HYDRATION_BASICS.body: On any hike you lose water through sweat and breathing, faster in heat and at elevation. Aim for at least half a liter per hour of activity, and drink steadily rather than waiting until you feel thirsty. By the time you notice thirst, you're already behind.

HYDRATION_DIURETICS.title: Hydration Interference
HYDRATION_DIURETICS.body: Diuretics like caffeine and alcohol tell your kidneys to release water. They can effectively 'cancel out' your hydration!

COTTON_CLOTHING_WARNING.title: Cotton Kills
COTTON_CLOTHING_WARNING.body: Cotton absorbs water and loses all insulation value when wet. In rain or snow, it leads to hypothermia. Choose Wool or Synthetic!

FIBER_ENERGY_STABILITY.title: Energy Stability
FIBER_ENERGY_STABILITY.body: High sugar without fiber causes insulin crashes. Fiber-rich whole foods provide the most stable fuel.

SODIUM_HYDRATION_LOAD.title: Sodium Balance
SODIUM_HYDRATION_LOAD.body: Sodium is essential for fluid balance and for helping your nerves and muscles work correctly, especially when you are sweating on the trail. The problem is balance: too little sodium can hurt performance, but too much sodium without enough water can leave you thirstier and make hydration harder to manage. In PACK OUT, this lesson shows up when your pack is both very salty and short on effective hydration, which means you need a better mix of water and lower-sodium foods.

WHOLE_FOOD_FUEL.title: Whole Food Power
WHOLE_FOOD_FUEL.body: Minimally processed plant foods are nutrient-dense and high in antioxidants, helping your muscles recover faster from the trail!

PACK_WEIGHT_RATIO.title: The 20% Rule
PACK_WEIGHT_RATIO.body: Try to keep your total pack weight under 20% of your body weight. This reduces the mechanical strain on your joints.

LEAVE_NO_TRACE_VIOLATION.title: Leave No Trace
LEAVE_NO_TRACE_VIOLATION.body: Packing items that create waste without bringing a way to pack it out harms the environment. Always pack a trash bag or Ziploc!

VOLUME_OVERFLOW.title: Packing Efficiency
VOLUME_OVERFLOW.body: A backpack only has so much space! High-volume items like bags of chips fill your pack quickly, leaving no room for essentials.

TEN_ESSENTIALS_MISSING.title: The 10 Essentials
TEN_ESSENTIALS_MISSING.body: Always carry navigation, sun protection, insulation, illumination, first-aid, fire, tools, shelter, food, and water. The trail doesn't care about your plans.
